title: Optimistic decode: model onboarding guidelines, metrics, and rollback
content:
Summary:
This doc captures a pragmatic onboarding/playbook for integrating models that use optimistic (speculative) decoding paths into Redwood’s serving runtime. It focuses on acceptance criteria, telemetry and success metrics, safe rollback gates, kernel/scheduler considerations, and KV-cache warmup strategies.

Goals / non-goals:
- Goal: Provide a repeatable, low-risk path for model teams to enable optimistic decode features (early-token generation, lookahead kernels, or speculative next-step proposals) while preserving latency SLOs and cost targets.
- Goal: Define concrete metrics and thresholds for canary→ramp→full rollout and an automated rollback surface.
- Non-goal: Decide for a specific kernel implementation; this doc is implementation-agnostic but requires measurable signals.

Definitions (quick):
- optimistic decode: serving technique where the runtime predicts/starts generating subsequent tokens on a fast, approximate path and reconciles with the authoritative path when available. Includes early-kernel passes, reduced-precision streams, or heuristic proposals.
- reconciler: component that verifies speculative tokens against canonical outputs and gates commit.
- KV-cache warmup: pre-populating key/value caches or maintaining persistent KV shards for lower first-token latency.

Scope and integration points:
- Serving runtime hooks: kernel routing, batch scheduler, request router, reconciler hooks, observability events.
- Model onboarding data: per-model metadata (expected seq_len distribution, quantization profile, checkpoint id).
- Rollout orchestration: Redwood Console policy application (canary %, ramp plan), alerting and automated fallback.

High-level onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1) Local validation (model team): unit tests that run optimistic and canonical inference on 1000 prompts (diverse lengths) and assert semantic divergence rate <= X (see metrics). Smoke perf tests against local runtime.
2) Artifact tagging: push model variant with metadata fields: optimistic_enabled: true, optimistic_profile: <profile-id>, kv_persistent: boolean, kernel_hint: <hint>.
3) Canary configuration: create canary route with 2% of traffic and dedicated canary pool (if possible). Set exploratory cost limits (token budget) and enable detailed trace logs.
4) Load test: run synthetic load matching p95 request concurrency for 30m with canary config. Validate resource isolation and cost delta.
5) Observability baseline: capture 48h baseline of latency/cost/quality for canonical model; store baseline in canary dashboard.
6) Canary run + gating evaluation: run live canary for 24–72h or until N requests (configurable). Evaluate gates below.
7) Ramp or rollback: if gates pass, follow ramp plan; otherwise, rollback with automated steps (see rollback).

Acceptance criteria and gating signals (must pass to progress):
- Latency SLOs: p50/p90/p99 tail for token generation must be within configured SLO delta relative to baseline. Outright failure if p99 increases > 30% or p50 > baseline + 15ms absolute (values configurable per team).
- Cost per 1k tokens: delta must be <= +25% during canary or justified by quality improvements. Can be overridden for experimental tests.
- Quality divergence: semantic divergence (fraction of tokens where canonical != speculative commit) must be <= 1.5% on the evaluation prompt set. Behavioral divergence (measured via task-specific evals — e.g., pass@k, BLEU, Rouge where applicable) must be within 2% absolute.
- Reconciler consistency: rollback reconciliation rate (cases where reconciler discards speculative tokens) must be <= 2% at steady state. Spikes during warmup acceptable if transient and < 6% lasting < 1h.
- Error budget burn: error rate (5xx, internal reconciler errors, mismatched commit states) must not exceed 0.1% of requests over canary window.
- Observability completeness: traces must include kernel selection, scheduler decisions, KV-cache hit/miss, reconcile decisions, and commit latency. No rollout unless traces are consistently populated.
- Safety checks: model must pass content-safety quick checks (internal sanitizer) at canary. If model fails, reject automatically.

Primary metrics to collect (examples / names used in runtime):
- infer.latency.token.p50, .p90, .p99 (ms)
- infer.cost.per_1k_tokens (USD estimate)
- optimistic.reconcile.rate (fraction of reconciles that cause mismatch)
- optimistic.discard.rate (fraction of speculative tokens discarded)
- kvcache.hit_ratio by sequence prefix
- kernel.route.count by kernel_hint
- scheduler.batch.size.avg and stddev
- errors.reconciler, errors.kernels, errors.kv
- user-visible.failure_rate (5xx returned to caller)
- quality.eval.delta.<task> (model-specific eval metric)

Kernel and scheduler considerations (operational guidance):
- Kernel hints: model metadata should supply a hint (e.g., "float16-fast-attn", "quant-q4_1", "spec-lite") and the runtime will map to supported kernel builds. The runtime must record kernel mismatch events (when selected kernel differs from hint).
- Prefer kernel compatibility checks at admission time: if a model requests an unsupported speculative kernel on a pool, block the rollout and mark as incompatible.
- Scheduler interactions: optimistic decode increases intra-request concurrency (parallel kernel runs for speculation + authoritative path). Scheduler must:
  - limit concurrency per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbor when speculative backfills occur;
  - prioritize canonical commit path for low-latency SLA traffic;
  - permit speculative work at lower priority with preemptible GPU slices or isolated slots.
- Batching strategy: allow speculative work to be continuously batched but cap speculative batch size if it causes canonical path delay. Monitor scheduler.batch.wait_time and speculative.latency.

KV-cache warmup and persistence patterns:
- Warmup strategies: proactive prefix prefetch (based on route heuristics), lightweight approximate warmup (use compressed KV snapshots), and background async prefetch driven by request queues.
- Persistence: team must declare kv_persistent boolean. If true, the dedicated pool will keep KV shards resident across requests; autoscaler policies must treat these nodes as stateful.
- Metrics: kvcache.load_time_ms, kvcache.prefetch.success_rate, kvcache.eviction_rate. If kvcache.eviction_rate spikes during canary, expect degraded speculative success.

Rollback plan (automated + manual):
Automated triggers (immediate rollback if any trigger fires):
- user-visible.failure_rate > 0.2% sustained for 10 minutes
- p99 latency > threshold (see gates) for 5 consecutive 1m windows
- reconciler.discard_rate > 8% for 15 minutes
- Safety detector flagged content-safety failures > 1 per 1000 requests

Automated rollback steps (runtime):
1) Pause canary routing: switch canary route to baseline model (atomic route swap).
2) Drain speculative tasks: reconcile outstanding speculative tasks with a special fast-path that avoids committing speculative outputs.
3) Scale back speculative-only kernel pools to zero and mark pool as failed for this model variant.
4) Emit rollback audit event with reason, metrics snapshot, and last 100 reconciler traces.
5) Trigger paging to on-call SRE + model owner.

Manual remediation checklist (post-rollback):
- Collect sample traces for failed windows and annotate top 10 latencies and reconcile mismatches.
- Run controlled replay to reproduce mismatch locally with same kernel/scheduler config.
- If root cause is kernel incompatibility or scheduler starvation, tag model variant incompatible and require remediation before re-onboarding.
- If root cause is model quality (semantic divergence), require model team to update checkpoint or revert optimistic flag.

Observability and dashboarding recommendations:
- Create a model-specific dashboard during canary that overlays baseline vs canary for all primary metrics.
- Drilldowns: reconciler event timeline, per-kernel latency histograms, KV-cache hit maps keyed by prefix length, request/response diffs for mismatches.
- Trace sampling: sample 100% of reconciler events during first 30m of canary, then 5% for steady state.

Testing harness and synthetic validation:
- Unit harness: per-model harness that can run canonical & optimistic paths deterministically given a set of seed tokens. Store seeds in model artifact and run on CI.
- Load harness: synthetic clients that emulate real p50/p90 traffic shapes. Run with canary config for at least 30–60 minutes under 1.2x expected concurrency.
- Chaos tests: induce KV eviction, kernel OOM, and scheduler preemption during canary to validate graceful degradation.

Data retention and postmortem artifacts:
- Keep reconciler traces and last-50 mismatches for 90 days for debugging.
- Store canary snapshots (metrics and config) as immutable artifacts linked to model variant id.

Runbook snippets (quick commands and notes):
- To pause canary: /api/admin/route/swap?route_id=CANARY&target=baseline
- To fetch last mismatches: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.int/ops/model-mismatches?model=MODEL_ID&limit=100
- To force fallback on a pool: PATCH /api/pools/POOL_ID {"accept_speculative":false} (internal only)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide canonical thresholds for p99 increase that are acceptable per tier (free-tier vs enterprise-SLA).
- Can reconciler work be partially offloaded to CPU in a hybrid flow to reduce GPU contention? Need performance experiments.
- Would a token-level priority queue in scheduler reduce tail latency for canonical commits? Prototype required.
- Investigate whether model-level kv_persistent hints should be auto-suggested by Optimize based on observed prefix reuse.

Appendix A — example canary ramp (recommended):
- Canary: 2% traffic for 24h or 100k requests (whichever comes first). If all gates pass:
  - Stage 1: 10% for 6h, evaluate metrics
  - Stage 2: 30% for 12h, evaluate metrics
  - Stage 3: 60% for 12h, evaluate metrics
  - Full: 100%
Any stage that fails a gate triggers automated rollback and investigator paging.

Appendix B — minimum telemetry events (must be emitted by runtime):
- event.optimistic.decision {model, request_id, kernel_hint, speculative_batch_id, time_ms}
- event.optimistic.reconcile {request_id, reconcile_latency_ms, mismatch, discarded_tokens}
- event.kernel.selection {request_id, kernel_name, reason}
- event.kv.prefetch {request_id, success, duration_ms}

Owners and contacts:

- Secondary: Marco Li (applied-ml), Daniel Ortega (sre), Priya Sharma (platform)

If anything is unclear or you want a shorter checklist for handoff to CS or solutions engineering, ping me in #serving-runtime or open INF task in Jira (linked above).

Notes: draft — intentionally conservative thresholds to reduce risk. Will iterate after first two model onboards.
